div.l: And þus with feynyng flat̉eryng and Iapys
He made the ꝑpersoıı̄un and peple Apys
But truly to tellen at the laste
He was in Chirche a noble Ecclesiaste
Weel coude he rede a lessoıı̄un or a storye
But altherbest he song a Offertorye
For weel he wost whan that song was Sungge
He must preche and weel fyle hise tungge
To wynne syluer as he weel coude
Therfore he song full merely and loude
Now haue I tolde sothely in a clause
The estate the array þe noumbre and eke þe cause
Why that assembled was this companye
In Southwerk in this gentill hostelerye
That hight the Tabard fast by the belle
But now is tyme to yow to telle
How that we beren̄ vs that nyght
Whan we were in that hostelrye a lyght
And after wole I tellen̄ of oure Viage
And all the remenaunt of oure pilgrymage
But first I preye yow of your curtesye
That ye rette it nat my Vilanye
Though þat I pleynely speke in this matier
To tellen̄ yow ther wordis and ther chier
Ne though I speke ther wordis proprely
For this ye knowen Als weel as I
Who so shall tellen a tale after a man̄
He mot reherse as nygh as euer he can̄
Eủeryche woord if it be in his charge
All speke he neủer so rudely and large
Or elles he mote telle his tale ontrue
Or feyne thyngges or fynde woordꝭes newe
He may nat spare all if he were his brother
He mote asweel sey one woord as an other
Criste spake hym self full brode in holy writ
And weel ye wote no vylanye is it
Eke plato seith who so can hym rede
The woordys mote be cosyn to the dede
Also I praye you foryeve it me
Alle have I nat set folk in ther degree
Here in this tale as that shuld stonde
My witte is short ye may weel vnderstonde
Grete cheer our oste vs eủerycheon̄
And to soper sette he vs a non̄
He ʆserued vs with vitaile at the best
Strong was the wyne and wel drynk vs lest
A semely man oure oste was with all
For to be Marchale in an hall
A large man̄ he was with eyen̄ stepe
A Fayrer burgeys is non in Chepe
Bolde of hise speche and wyse and wele y taught
And of manhode hym lakked right naught
Ekke ther to he was right mery man̄
And after soper pleyen̄ he bygan̄
And spake of merthe a mong other thyngges
And whan that we had made our rekenyngges
And seid thus now lordyngges truly
Ye ben̄ to me welcome right hertely
For by my trouth if þat I shal nat lye
I seye nat this yeer so mery a companye
At ones in this herborwe as is now
Fayn wold I do you m̉erthe wost I how
And of a merthe I am right now by thought
To doon̄ you ease and it shall cost nought
Ye gon̄ to Canturbury god yow spede
The blysfull Martir acquite you your mede
And wele I wote as ye go by the weye
And shapen̄ you to talen̄ and to pleye
For truly confort ne m̉erthe is ther none
To ryde by the weye dombe as a stone
And therfor wole I maken you disporte
As I seid arst and done you som conforte
And if yow liketh alle by one assente
Forto stonden̄ at my Iugemente
And for to werken̄ as I shall yow seye
To morwen̄ when we ryden̄ by the weye
Now by my Fadres soule that is dede
But ye be mery I wole yeve you myne hede
Holde vp your hondes with out more speche
Oure counsell was nat long for to seche
Vs thought it was nat worth to make it no uyse
And graunted it hym with out more aduyse
And badde hym seye hise veredicte as hym lyste
Lordyngges qᵈuod he now herkeneth for the beste
But take it nat I praye you in disdeigne
This is þe poynte to speke short and pleyne
That eche of yow to shorte other the weye
In this viage shall tellen tales tweye
